anomalies.observed: The netlist contains two different ATtiny microcontrollers, U3 and U4, and every corresponding MCU pin is tied to the same net: U3.1/U4.1 on NET0005, U3.2/U4.2 on NET0003, U3.3/U4.3 on NET0001, U3.4/U4.4 on GND, U3.5/U4.5 on NET0002, U3.6/U4.6 on NET0004, U3.7/U4.7 on NET0011, and U3.8/U4.8 on +5V.
anomalies.expected: The design is described as an ATtiny-driven fan controller, which implies a single MCU driving the fan/ISP/I2C signals. If U4 were only an alternate footprint, it should be marked unpopulated/excluded; as presented, a second MCU is wired in parallel with the first.
anomalies.impact: If both footprints are populated, the two MCUs will contend on all shared GPIO/ISP/I2C nets, causing reset/programming conflicts and possible driver contention or damage. If only one MCU is intended, the netlist still includes an extra component that should not be assembled.

parsed.summary: The connectivity is otherwise internally consistent, but the netlist shows two different ATtiny MCUs wired pin-for-pin together, which is not a normal single-MCU fan-controller implementation and is likely an extra/parallel component anomaly.
